Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
9 October 2026 .
Brent $ 103.08 + 0.19 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Caspian Post and Yeni Şafak 1News.az reports several tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, per Iranian state media.

02 Brent stood at $103.08, up 0.19% over 24 hours, as of 06:28 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
Operational pressure in the Strait of Hormuz intensified overnight as Iranian state media, relayed by Caspian Post and Yeni Şafak English, reported that several tankers struck mines in the waterway. gCaptain reports a chemical tanker was hit by multiple projectiles off the coast of Qatar, with casualties among the crew; the Acers, which BBC News identified as the vessel struck in that area, was first carried in this feed on October 8, and the Qatar attack adds reported crew casualties as the latest development on that ship. Al Jazeera, relaying an Iranian claim, reports that IRGC forces say they target vessels nightly in the strait, with Fars citing unnamed military sources. Haaretz reports tanker attacks in the strait hit a record weekly high since the war began, and Dawn reports strait traffic has hit a two-month low following the attacks. Separately, Saudi Arabia is in talks to formalize Hormuz shuttle arrangements for market share, per gCaptain, though no agreement has been reported. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; the feed indexed 43 headlines in the last 24 hours. Brent traded at $103.08, up 0.19% over 24 hours, as of 06:28 UTC. As of 06:20 UTC, 108 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
